title: NOS3: NASA's SmallSat Test Bench
description: NOS3 (NASA Operational Simulator for Small Satellites) is the hardware-in-the-loop test bench that lets smallsat teams run their real flight software against simulated hardware. Built around the NOS Engine with 42 and Trick dynamics plus cFS flight software, it catches interface bugs before launch. It is how small missions get big-mission test discipline.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The NOS Engine
description: The NOS Engine is the message-passing core: simulated hardware components (power, comms, ADCS) exchange packets over software buses that mimic the real ones — I2C, SPI, UART, SpaceWire. Flight software cannot tell it is not talking to hardware. Fidelity lives in the bus protocols.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Simulated Spacecraft Hardware
description: NOS3 simulates the spacecraft's hardware boxes: electrical power (batteries, solar), radios, reaction wheels, GPS receivers — each a software model with the same interface as the real unit. Swap the sim for hardware later without changing flight software. Interfaces are the contract.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: cFS Inside NOS3
description: NOS3 runs actual cFS flight software — the same apps that will fly — against the simulated hardware, so the test is the flight configuration with hardware swapped for models. App bugs, timing bugs, and configuration bugs all surface here. Test what you fly, fly what you test.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: 42 and Dynamics in the Loop
description: Spacecraft dynamics in NOS3 come from 42-class simulation: attitude and orbit truth drive the simulated sensors, and actuator commands flow back into the dynamics. The loop is closed through the flight software. GNC gets tested against physics, not stubs.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Ground System
description: NOS3 includes a ground-system side: command uplink, telemetry downlink, and COSMOS-style tooling to operate the simulated mission. Operators practice on the sim before they touch the real spacecraft. The ground team trains where mistakes are free.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Day-in-the-Life Testing
description: NOS3 runs day-in-the-life tests: the full mission timeline — deployments, burns, payload ops, eclipses — executed against the sim to prove the flight software handles the whole story. Timeline bugs are mission bugs; this is where they die. DITL is the dress rehearsal.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Fault Injection Campaigns
description: NOS3 injects hardware faults — a stuck wheel, a dead radio, a brownout — to prove the flight software's fault responses work. FDIR logic that never sees a fault in test will not handle one in flight. Campaigns enumerate the failure space systematically.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Timing and Real-Time Behavior
description: Flight software timing is verified in NOS3: scheduler slots, bus latencies, interrupt timing — all measured against requirements in the sim. A missed deadline in sim is a finding; on orbit it is an anomaly. Real-time behavior is a requirement, not a hope.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: SmallSat Missions Using HIL
description: Smallsat missions adopt NOS3-class HIL to punch above their mass class: CubeSats running tested flight software with proven fault handling. The cost of a bug found in HIL is hours; on orbit it can be the mission. Test discipline scales down even when spacecraft do.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: From Sim to FlatSat to Flight
title: From Sim to FlatSat to Flight
description: The maturation path: NOS3 sim, then FlatSat (real avionics on a bench wired to sims), then flight. Each step replaces models with hardware while flight software stays constant. By launch, the software has met reality in stages. No surprises is the goal.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Regression Testing
description: Every flight software change re-runs the NOS3 regression suite — the safety net that catches what the change broke. Regressions run in CI so broken builds never reach the bench. The suite grows with the mission; it is an asset, not overhead.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Power System Simulation
description: NOS3's power models — solar input vs orbit, battery charge/discharge, load switching — prove the mission never goes power-negative. Eclipse seasons are the stress test. Power is life; the sim proves the budget closes.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Comms and Link Simulation
description: NOS3 simulates the RF link — passes, data rates, dropouts — so the mission proves it can get its data down. Store-and-forward, contact scheduling, and link budgets all get exercised. A spacecraft that cannot phone home is a very expensive brick.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The NOS3 Test Campaign End to End
description: Ladder-top NOS3: build the sim, load flight software, run DITL, inject faults, check timing, regress every change, mature sim to FlatSat to flight. Fifteen rungs from models to a smallsat that behaves like a flagship.
